cells.tense: The pattern is in your hands right now and you're steady about it — you know which shape is worth keeping and you keep it without gripping.
cells.ask: Offer the pattern to one person this week and take what they do with it as the return half — and notice whether the gesture settles you or unsteadies you.
cells.core:
The shape of what changed is clear to you and it holds. You can walk a whole day without testing it, and the ones you show it to get it quickly, because you're not asking anyone to applaud — the thing stands on its own. The pattern sits in the open in your ordinary days, and people move around it naturally.

The growing edge is the other half of the exchange. You take in what people give back — a question, a correction, a counter-shape — without counting what you're owed. Being straight about a share and holding a shape aren't the same job; today they can sit in the same hand. What comes back loosens something instead of tightening the grip.
cells.sheetLine: The shape is clear and you're keeping it without gripping.
cells.verb: hold steady the shape of what the change left behind
cells.place: in the mind that keeps the shape but can set the thing itself down

cells.tense: You're already guarding a pattern against versions of it that haven't arrived — bracing for the copies, the edits, the people who'll get it wrong.
cells.ask: Hand the pattern to someone who'll use it differently than you would, and let their version stand today without correcting it.
cells.core:
You've been reading the pattern ahead of schedule. Sit in one conversation about it and it turns into a test of whether the other person sees the same mechanism — and the shape actually lives in what they pull toward and away from, not in the perimeter you've drawn around it.

The shape stays true when the versions around it aren't seen as threats. What you might be protecting isn't the pattern but the fact that you found it — handing it over feels like losing the credit, not like the shape surviving contact. Nothing's been taken yet, and the next conversation doesn't need a verdict.

cells.tense: The pattern is still standing there and you're back at the wall you built for it — at the last door, from before, where you stood with the shape in your hands and then stopped standing.
cells.ask: Pick one person and send the shape as it is, unfinished, one sentence — and let the act itself be the movement here.
cells.core:
This works when a shape gets a small clear push — one sentence, one person, no verdict required. You can tell a pattern twenty times inside your head and it doesn't get tested; the moment it goes to a living reader, something in it either holds or cracks, and either result is worth more than the next rehearsal. That's the shape's natural life: built, shown, adjusted.

The pattern isn't missing. Direction is. What's behind the wall is shaped exactly enough to travel — you can tell someone its outline right now, badly, and see what they do with it. The stopping isn't about whether the shape is ready; it's about what happened the last time one went out. Push the shape instead of the sending; the door reopens from that side.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern is ready and you've stopped walking it through the door.

cells.tense: You're already the one holding the pattern for the whole room, and you talk about it like it arrived on its own — the claim on it has slipped somewhere out of view.
cells.ask: Write this sentence and finish it: the shape here is mine because ____. Say it once out loud.
cells.core:
You're the reason the pattern is available at all — the conversations you've had, the hard-won clarity, the questions you keep asking that made the shape visible. People walk out with it in their hands and you describe it as if it fell into place. What holds up here is that the shape is real; what's missing is the sentence that says you're the one who found it.

That claim doesn't have to be dramatic. It can be a plain statement of who did this work, said without heat, and it does real work: the next time the pattern gets copied or misread, the one who named it can speak. You're not taking credit; you're setting the record straight before someone else does.
